name: Max Verstappen
vibe_embedding_text: Max Verstappen is a three-time Formula 1 World Champion and the most dominant driver of the current era. Aggressive Dutch racing driver known for his uncompromising overtaking style, fiery team radio messages, and relentless competitiveness. Won three consecutive championships (2021-2023). Famous for saying 'simply lovely' after wins and the 'inchident' meme. Races with raw intensity and refuses to yield position.

name: Lewis Hamilton
vibe_embedding_text: Lewis Hamilton is the seven-time Formula 1 World Champion, the joint-most successful driver in history. British racing driver who drove for McLaren (2007-2012) and Mercedes (2013-2024, 12 seasons). Known for 'hammer time' qualifying laps, fashion-forward lifestyle, social activism, and incredible wet-weather driving. Dominated the turbo-hybrid era with Mercedes from 2014-2020.

name: Kimi Räikkönen
memes: leave me alone I know what I'm doing
vibe_embedding_text: Kimi Räikkönen is the ultimate emotionless, ice-cold Finnish racing driver and 2007 World Champion. Drove for Sauber (2001), McLaren (2002-2006, 5 seasons), Ferrari (2007-2009, 2014-2018, 8 seasons total), Lotus (2012-2013), and Alfa Romeo (2019-2021). Famous for monosyllabic 'bwoah', hating media interviews, eating ice cream on the grid, and 'leave me alone I know what I'm doing'.

name: Daniel Ricciardo
vibe_embedding_text: Daniel Ricciardo is the smiling, party-loving Australian racing driver nicknamed the Honey Badger. Famous for celebrating podiums by drinking champagne from his racing shoe (the 'shoey'), his enormous infectious grin, late-braking divebombs, and bringing joy to the paddock. Fierce racer disguised behind a carefree personality.

name: Carlos Sainz
vibe_embedding_text: Carlos Sainz is a calm, consistent, strategic Spanish racing driver known as the Smooth Operator. Methodical racer who maximizes results through intelligence rather than raw aggression. Loves spicy food, known for his work ethic and ability to extract performance from difficult cars.

name: Charles Leclerc
memes: plan B plan C plan D
vibe_embedding_text: Charles Leclerc is an emotional, self-critical Monegasque racing driver destined for Ferrari greatness. Famous for frustrated radio messages like 'we are checking' and 'nooo', beautiful qualifying laps, playing piano, and carrying the weight of Ferrari's championship hopes with honest vulnerability.

name: Lando Norris
vibe_embedding_text: Lando Norris is a funny, self-deprecating British racing driver who streams video games on Twitch and runs the Quadrant gaming brand. Gen-Z energy with rapid pace on track, known for his humor on social media, close friendship with other young drivers, and mental health openness.

name: Oscar Piastri
memes: I understand, I will not be driving for Alpine
vibe_embedding_text: Oscar Piastri is a deadpan, unbothered Australian rookie who channels Kimi-like indifference. Famously rejected Alpine's contract announcement with a blunt social media post. Mark Webber's protégé who races with ice-cold composure beyond his years and responds to everything with 'looks good'.

name: George Russell
vibe_embedding_text: George Russell is a methodical, meticulous British racing driver known as Mr Saturday for his incredible qualifying pace. Famous for preparing detailed PowerPoint presentations for team meetings, writing structured arguments, and crashing behind the safety car at Imola. Combines corporate precision with genuine speed.

name: Fernando Alonso
vibe_embedding_text: Fernando Alonso is an obsessive, never-surrendering Spanish racing veteran and two-time World Champion. Drove for Minardi, Renault (2003-2006, 2008-2009), McLaren (2007, 2015-2018), Ferrari (2010-2014, 5 seasons), Alpine (2021-2022), and Aston Martin (2023-present). Master of defensive driving and extracting miracles from bad cars. Famous for 'GP2 engine' radio rant, 'El Plan' meme, and racing competitively into his 40s.

name: Sebastian Vettel
vibe_embedding_text: Sebastian Vettel is a four-time Formula 1 World Champion. German racing driver who drove for Toro Rosso (2007-2008), Red Bull Racing (2009-2014, 6 seasons), Ferrari (2015-2020, 6 seasons), and Aston Martin (2021-2022). Won four consecutive championships with Red Bull. Later became beloved for activism protecting bees, picking up litter, and speaking on human rights. Famous for 'multi 21' drama and 'grazie ragazzi' celebrations.

name: Sergio Pérez
vibe_embedding_text: Sergio Pérez is a patient, reliable Mexican racing driver known as Checo. The Minister of Defense for his incredible ability to hold position and manage tyres over long stints. Street circuit specialist who extracts maximum performance from difficult conditions through calm, calculated racecraft.

name: Valtteri Bottas
vibe_embedding_text: Valtteri Bottas is a blunt, dry-humored Finnish racing driver. Drove for Williams (2013-2016, 4 seasons), Mercedes (2017-2021, 5 seasons), and Alfa Romeo/Stake (2022-present). Famous for his iconic mullet hairstyle, love of coffee, and naked cycling photos. Known for the defiant 'to whom it may concern' radio message.

name: Nico Rosberg
vibe_embedding_text: Nico Rosberg is the analytical German driver who famously retired immediately after winning his only world championship in 2016, defeating Lewis Hamilton through sheer psychological warfare and meticulous preparation. Known for the dramatic cap-throwing incident and choosing family over further racing glory.

name: Jenson Button
vibe_embedding_text: Jenson Button is a smooth, relaxed British world champion known for exceptional wet-weather driving ability. Won the 2009 title with Brawn GP in a fairytale season. Famous for his silky smooth driving style, triathlon fitness, laid-back personality, and ability to read changing conditions better than anyone.

name: Michael Schumacher
vibe_embedding_text: Michael Schumacher is a seven-time Formula 1 World Champion, the most dominant driver of his era. Relentless German racing legend who drove for Benetton (1991-1995) and Ferrari (1996-2006, 11 seasons), then briefly Mercedes (2010-2012). Known for his superhuman work ethic, psychological dominance over rivals, controversial racing tactics, and building Ferrari's greatest dynasty from 2000-2004.

name: Ayrton Senna
vibe_embedding_text: Ayrton Senna is the intense, spiritual Brazilian racing legend considered by many the greatest driver ever. Three-time champion who drove for Toleman (1984), Lotus (1985-1987), McLaren (1988-1993, 6 seasons — his iconic team), and Williams (1994). Known for supernatural wet-weather ability, Monaco dominance, deep religious faith, and tragic death at Imola 1994.

name: Alain Prost
vibe_embedding_text: Alain Prost is the calculated, strategic French racing legend nicknamed The Professor. Four-time World Champion who drove for Renault (1981-1983), McLaren (1984-1989, 6 seasons), Ferrari (1990-1991), and Williams (1993). Won through intelligence, smoothness, and minimal risk. Famous rivalry with Senna defined an era.

name: Mika Häkkinen
vibe_embedding_text: Mika Häkkinen is a quiet, fast, respectful Finnish racing champion. Two-time World Champion who drove for Lotus (1991-1992) and McLaren (1993-2001, 9 seasons). Known as The Flying Finn, defeated Schumacher with pure speed and sportsmanship. Famous for crying behind a barrier after a spin, and going on a permanent 'sabbatical'.

name: Nico Hülkenberg
vibe_embedding_text: Nico Hülkenberg is an unlucky, honest German driver who held the record for most race starts without a podium finish. Known for incredible one-lap pace, the ability to jump into any car as a super-substitute and immediately perform, and being perpetually underrated by the paddock despite obvious talent.

name: Pierre Gasly
vibe_embedding_text: Pierre Gasly is an emotional, resilient French racing driver with the ultimate redemption story. Demoted from Red Bull then won at Monza with AlphaTauri in a stunning miracle victory. Known for wearing his heart on his sleeve, raw emotional radio celebrations, and proving every doubter wrong.

name: Rubens Barrichello
vibe_embedding_text: Rubens Barrichello is the loyal, long-suffering Brazilian driver. Drove for Jordan (1993-1996), Stewart (1997-1999), Ferrari (2000-2005, 6 seasons as Schumacher's number two), Honda/Brawn (2006-2009), and Williams (2010-2011). Forever associated with team orders and finishing second. Held the record for most race starts.

name: Damon Hill
vibe_embedding_text: Damon Hill is the son of legendary double champion Graham Hill who carved his own path to become 1996 World Champion. Overcame immense pressure of family legacy and controversial 1994 title battle with Schumacher. Quiet determination personified, proving himself as a champion in his own right.

name: Jacques Villeneuve
vibe_embedding_text: Jacques Villeneuve is an outspoken, fearless Canadian driver and son of legendary Gilles Villeneuve. 1997 World Champion known for bold overtaking moves, controversial opinions, bleached hair, and refusing to conform to F1's corporate expectations. Brought IndyCar aggression to Formula 1.

name: Nigel Mansell
vibe_embedding_text: Nigel Mansell is the fearless, mustachioed British racing champion known as Il Leone (The Lion). Drove for Lotus (1980-1984), Williams (1985-1988, 1991-1992, 1994 — his most iconic team, 7 seasons total), and Ferrari (1989-1990). 1992 World Champion with Williams. Famous for aggressive racing style, massive crowd appeal, and being the working-class hero of British motorsport.

name: Kimi Antonelli
vibe_embedding_text: Kimi Antonelli is the Italian teenage prodigy and Mercedes wonderkid who broke age records throughout junior formula. Named after Kimi Räikkönen, signed by Mercedes as their future star. Represents the next generation of F1 talent with blistering pace beyond his years.

name: Nikita Mazepin
vibe_embedding_text: Nikita Mazepin is the controversial Russian pay driver infamous for constant spinning during his single F1 season, earning the nickname Mazespin. Known for off-track controversies, being last in nearly every race, and having his contract terminated due to geopolitical events.

name: Gabriel Bortoleto
vibe_embedding_text: Gabriel Bortoleto is the exciting young Brazilian racing talent carrying the hopes of 'Brazil is back' in Formula 1. F2 champion who earned his seat through merit, representing the next generation of Brazilian racing heritage after Senna, Barrichello, and Massa.

name: Alex Albon
vibe_embedding_text: Alex Albon is the likeable Thai-British racing driver famous for 'they race me so hard' radio message at Red Bull. Known for painting watercolors of cats, gentle personality off-track contrasting with strong racecraft, and rebuilding his career at Williams after being dropped by Red Bull.

name: Esteban Ocon
vibe_embedding_text: Esteban Ocon is a determined, stubborn French racing driver notorious for intense teammate rivalries. Clashed with Pérez at Force India and Gasly at Alpine. Known for never backing down, fighting for every position regardless of team dynamics, and a Hungary 2021 shock victory.

name: Yuki Tsunoda
vibe_embedding_text: Yuki Tsunoda is the fiery, passionate Japanese racing driver famous for explosive angry team radio outbursts about traffic and car problems. Known for his short stature, enormous aggression on track, and entertaining radio communications that capture pure racing frustration.

name: Kevin Magnussen
vibe_embedding_text: Kevin Magnussen is the brutally aggressive, outspoken Danish racing driver famous for telling Nico Hülkenberg to 'suck my balls' in a press conference. Known for uncompromising first-lap racing, making no apologies for hard driving, and being one of F1's most entertaining loose cannons.

name: Romain Grosjean
vibe_embedding_text: Romain Grosjean is the French-Swiss racing driver who miraculously survived a horrific fireball crash at Bahrain 2020, escaping a car split in half and engulfed in flames. Previously known for first-lap incidents, his survival story became one of F1's greatest miracles.

name: Mick Schumacher
vibe_embedding_text: Mick Schumacher is the German racing driver carrying the immense weight of being Michael Schumacher's son. F2 champion who struggled in F1 with Haas under enormous public pressure and scrutiny. Represents the challenge of living up to a legendary family name in motorsport.

name: Lance Stroll
vibe_embedding_text: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver known for surprising wet-weather ability and being the son of Aston Martin team owner Lawrence Stroll. Scored a podium at a very young age, genuinely quick in the rain, but forever associated with the 'pay driver' label despite real talent in changing conditions.

name: Zhou Guanyu
vibe_embedding_text: Zhou Guanyu is the first Chinese driver in Formula 1 history, pioneering representation for the world's largest country in motorsport. Known for his calm demeanor, survival of a terrifying Silverstone rollover crash, and opening doors for future Chinese racing talent.

name: Logan Sargeant
vibe_embedding_text: Logan Sargeant was the first American F1 driver in years, carrying the hopes of US fans into Formula 1 with Williams. Struggled against teammate Albon and was replaced mid-season, but represented the growing American interest in the sport during its Netflix-driven boom.

name: Nyck de Vries
vibe_embedding_text: Nyck de Vries is the Dutch Formula E champion who scored points on his surprise F1 debut at Monza but was fired from AlphaTauri after just a handful of races. The ultimate one-race wonder whose brief F1 career ended almost as soon as it began.

name: Antonio Giovinazzi
vibe_embedding_text: Antonio Giovinazzi is the Italian racing driver nicknamed 'Italian Jesus' for his flowing long hair and gentle demeanor. Raced for Alfa Romeo/Sauber with quiet competence, deeply religious, and represented Italy on the F1 grid with grace if not spectacular results.

name: Kamui Kobayashi
vibe_embedding_text: Kamui Kobayashi is the fearless Japanese racing driver famous for impossibly late divebomb overtakes on the final lap. A cult fan-favorite who attacked every corner with zero self-preservation, crowdfunded his seat, and provided some of F1's most entertaining wheel-to-wheel battles.

name: Daniil Kvyat
vibe_embedding_text: Daniil Kvyat is the Russian racing driver dubbed 'The Torpedo' by Sebastian Vettel for his aggressive first-corner moves. Infamously demoted from Red Bull to make way for Max Verstappen, becoming a cautionary tale of the Red Bull driver program's ruthlessness.

name: Jean-Éric Vergne
vibe_embedding_text: Jean-Éric Vergne is a French driver who won two Formula E electric racing titles (not F1 championships) after being overlooked by Red Bull for F1 promotion. Never won an F1 race or F1 championship.

name: Brendon Hartley
vibe_embedding_text: Brendon Hartley is a New Zealand racing driver who won the Le Mans 24 Hours and WEC Endurance title (not an F1 championship) after a brief, difficult spell in F1 with Toro Rosso. Never won an F1 race or championship.

name: Stoffel Vandoorne
vibe_embedding_text: Stoffel Vandoorne is the talented Belgian driver whose F1 career was destroyed by being paired with Fernando Alonso at a terrible McLaren. Despite being GP2 champion and clearly quick, he was overshadowed and dropped after two seasons, finding success later in Formula E.

name: Felipe Nasr
vibe_embedding_text: Felipe Nasr is the Brazilian driver who literally saved the Sauber team from financial collapse by scoring crucial points at the rain-soaked 2016 Brazilian Grand Prix. His ninth place was worth millions in constructors' championship prize money.

name: Pascal Wehrlein
vibe_embedding_text: Pascal Wehrlein is a German racing driver who won the DTM touring car title (not F1) as a Mercedes protégé but never got a top F1 seat. Never won an F1 race or F1 championship despite impressive junior results.

name: Marcus Ericsson
vibe_embedding_text: Marcus Ericsson is the Swedish driver immortalized by Charles Leclerc's sarcastic 'I think Ericsson hit us' radio message when Ericsson was nowhere near. Found success in IndyCar after F1 including winning the Indianapolis 500, proving his talent in a different series.

name: Adrian Sutil
vibe_embedding_text: Adrian Sutil is the German racing driver heartbreakingly robbed of a podium at Monaco 2008 when Kimi Räikkönen crashed into him while leading. A talented pianist off-track who showed genuine pace with Force India but never got the top-team opportunity.

name: Paul di Resta
vibe_embedding_text: Paul di Resta is the Scottish racing driver turned Sky Sports F1 commentator. DTM champion who had a solid if unspectacular F1 career with Force India before transitioning to television punditry where he's become a familiar voice in F1 broadcasting.

name: Heikki Kovalainen
vibe_embedding_text: Heikki Kovalainen is the underrated Finnish racing driver who won a race for McLaren but was overshadowed by teammate Lewis Hamilton. A genuinely quick driver who never quite got the sustained machinery to show his full potential in Formula 1.

name: Jarno Trulli
vibe_embedding_text: Jarno Trulli is the Italian racing driver famous for the 'Trulli Train' — qualifying brilliantly then driving slowly in the race, creating a frustrated queue of faster cars unable to pass. A genuine qualifying specialist who made his own wine.

name: Timo Glock
vibe_embedding_text: Timo Glock is the German racing driver forever associated with 'IS THAT GLOCK?!' — the iconic commentary moment from Brazil 2008 when he slowed on worn dry tyres in the rain, allowing Lewis Hamilton past to clinch the championship on the final corner of the final lap.

name: Nick Heidfeld
vibe_embedding_text: Nick Heidfeld is the German driver who holds the unwanted record of most podium finishes without ever winning a race. Nicknamed 'Quick Nick' for his consistent speed, he was the ultimate bridesmaid of F1 — always close but never quite getting that elusive victory.

name: Giancarlo Fisichella
vibe_embedding_text: Giancarlo Fisichella is the Italian racing driver who produced one of F1's greatest shocks by putting the Force India on the front row at Spa 2009 and nearly winning. A quick, likeable driver whose career highlight came when everyone least expected it.

name: Robert Kubica
vibe_embedding_text: Robert Kubica is the Polish racing driver whose trajectory to world champion was derailed by a horrific rally crash that partially severed his arm. The ultimate 'what if' of modern F1 — on the verge of a Ferrari seat before injury, then made an emotional one-armed comeback years later.

name: Pastor Maldonado
vibe_embedding_text: Pastor Maldonado is the chaotic Venezuelan driver known as 'Crashdonado' for his incredible ability to crash into anything and everything. Somehow won the 2012 Spanish Grand Prix in a Williams then set fire to his garage. The most entertaining and unpredictable driver of his era.

name: Vitaly Petrov
vibe_embedding_text: Vitaly Petrov is the first Russian F1 driver, forever famous for holding off Fernando Alonso at Abu Dhabi 2010, directly costing Alonso the world championship. His defensive driving in that single race changed F1 history and handed Vettel the title.

name: Jérôme d'Ambrosio
vibe_embedding_text: Jérôme d'Ambrosio is the Belgian driver who had a brief, quiet F1 career with Virgin Racing before finding more success and longevity in Formula E. Represented Belgium on the F1 grid without much fanfare.

name: Narain Karthikeyan
vibe_embedding_text: Narain Karthikeyan is the first Indian Formula 1 driver, pioneering Indian representation in the sport. Raced for backmarker teams but opened the door for Indian motorsport and inspired a generation of Indian racing fans.

name: Pedro de la Rosa
vibe_embedding_text: Pedro de la Rosa is the Spanish driver who spent most of his career as McLaren's trusted test and development driver. The ultimate behind-the-scenes contributor who helped develop championship-winning cars while rarely getting to race them himself.

name: Bruno Senna
vibe_embedding_text: Bruno Senna is the nephew of legendary Ayrton Senna who carried the famous family name into Formula 1. Showed flashes of talent at Williams but ultimately couldn't escape the shadow of his uncle's legacy in the sport's most storied dynasty.

name: Lucas di Grassi
vibe_embedding_text: Lucas di Grassi is the Brazilian driver who became a Formula E legend and sustainability champion. Won the inaugural Formula E title race and became one of electric racing's most prominent advocates, combining racing with environmental activism.

name: Karun Chandhok
vibe_embedding_text: Karun Chandhok is the Indian racing driver turned respected Sky Sports F1 analyst. Had a brief F1 career but found his true calling as one of the sport's most knowledgeable and articulate television pundits, bringing deep technical insight to broadcasts.

name: Sakon Yamamoto
vibe_embedding_text: Sakon Yamamoto is the Japanese driver known primarily as an unexpected substitute and fill-in driver for backmarker teams. Made sporadic F1 appearances without leaving a major mark, representing Japan's motorsport funding model.

name: Jean Alesi
vibe_embedding_text: Jean Alesi is the passionate French-Sicilian driver who became a Ferrari cult hero despite winning only one race. His emotional, aggressive driving style and genuine love for the Scuderia made him beloved by tifosi even without championships. The romantic racer of his generation.

name: Gerhard Berger
vibe_embedding_text: Gerhard Berger is the Austrian racing driver famous as F1's greatest prankster and Ayrton Senna's closest friend. Known for elaborate practical jokes including hiding Senna's passport, setting fire to his briefcase, and once putting a snake in someone's hotel room. Fast and funny.

name: Heinz-Harald Frentzen
vibe_embedding_text: Heinz-Harald Frentzen is a fast German driver who came close to winning in 1999 with Jordan before mechanical failures robbed him. Never won a championship despite being one of the era's quickest, representing unfulfilled potential rather than championship glory.

name: Mika Salo
vibe_embedding_text: Mika Salo is the reliable Finnish substitute driver who famously stepped into Michael Schumacher's Ferrari seat and was asked to let Eddie Irvine win to help the championship fight. A solid, dependable driver respected throughout the paddock.

name: Johnny Herbert
vibe_embedding_text: Johnny Herbert is the British underdog racing driver who won three Grands Prix despite career-threatening leg injuries from a junior formula crash. His victory at Silverstone 1995 was one of the most emotional moments in British motorsport history.

name: Olivier Panis
vibe_embedding_text: Olivier Panis is the French driver who produced one of F1's greatest shocks by winning the 1996 Monaco Grand Prix for Ligier in chaotic wet conditions. Only three cars finished and Panis was the one holding the trophy in one of racing's most unlikely victories.

name: Riccardo Patrese
vibe_embedding_text: Riccardo Patrese is the Italian racing driver who held the record for most Grand Prix starts for many years. Known for incredible longevity and consistency across multiple eras of F1, racing competitively from the late 1970s into the early 1990s.

name: Michele Alboreto
vibe_embedding_text: Michele Alboreto is the Italian driver who fought Alain Prost for the 1985 World Championship with Ferrari before reliability failures crushed his title hopes. A true gentleman racer and one of Italy's finest drivers of the 1980s.

name: Ivan Capelli
vibe_embedding_text: Ivan Capelli is the Italian driver who nearly won the 1990 French Grand Prix in the tiny Leyton House March — one of F1's greatest David vs Goliath stories. Led the race before mechanical problems denied him a miracle victory for a minnow team.

name: Ukyo Katayama
vibe_embedding_text: Ukyo Katayama is the Japanese racing driver who later became a mountaineer and adventurer, climbing some of the world's highest peaks. Known in F1 for brave but sometimes crash-prone driving and later for his incredible physical adventures after retirement.

name: Jos Verstappen
vibe_embedding_text: Jos Verstappen is the Dutch racing driver best known as the father of Max Verstappen. Had his own F1 career including the terrifying Benetton pit fire at Hockenheim 1994. Became famous for being Max's demanding karting father and mentor.

name: Pedro Lamy
vibe_embedding_text: Pedro Lamy is the Portuguese racing driver who pioneered his country's representation in Formula 1. Had a promising career interrupted by a severe testing crash but returned to race and later found success in sports car racing.

name: Luca Badoer
vibe_embedding_text: Luca Badoer is the Italian driver who served as Ferrari's loyal test driver for nearly a decade, developing championship-winning cars without racing them. When finally given a race seat as substitute in 2009, he struggled badly — the ultimate behind-the-scenes contributor.

name: Alessandro Zanardi
vibe_embedding_text: Alessandro Zanardi is the legendary Italian CART champion who lost both legs in a horrific racing accident, then reinvented himself as a Paralympic handcycling gold medalist. One of motorsport's most inspirational figures who refused to let tragedy define him.

name: Gianni Morbidelli
vibe_embedding_text: Gianni Morbidelli is the Italian driver who scored a surprise podium finish for the tiny Footwork team at the 1995 Australian Grand Prix. A journeyman racer who produced one memorable highlight for a backmarker team.

name: Arvid Lindblad
vibe_embedding_text: Arvid Lindblad is the British teenage prodigy in the Red Bull junior program who became one of the youngest F2 race winners. Tipped as a future F1 star with exceptional pace beyond his years in single-seater racing.

name: Théo Pourchaire
vibe_embedding_text: Théo Pourchaire is the talented young French driver who won the F2 championship but couldn't secure a full-time F1 seat, representing the cruel politics of modern F1's limited grid spots. One of the most unlucky career trajectories in recent junior formula history.

name: Felipe Drugovich
vibe_embedding_text: Felipe Drugovich is the Brazilian F2 champion serving as Aston Martin's reserve driver, waiting for his opportunity to race in Formula 1. Dominant in F2 but stuck in the reserve role, representing the frustrating path many champions face.

name: Frederik Vesti
vibe_embedding_text: Frederik Vesti is the Danish Mercedes junior driver who came tantalizingly close to reaching Formula 1. A consistent performer in junior categories who represents the many talented drivers just on the edge of the F1 grid.

name: Victor Martins
vibe_embedding_text: Victor Martins is the French Alpine academy driver and F3 champion working his way through the junior formula ladder. Part of Alpine's effort to develop French racing talent for their future F1 lineup.

name: Mario Andretti
vibe_embedding_text: Mario Andretti is the ultimate American racing legend — 1978 F1 World Champion, IndyCar champion, Daytona 500 winner. The most versatile driver in motorsport history who conquered every discipline. Italian-born American icon who defined what it means to be a complete racing driver.

name: Jody Scheckter
vibe_embedding_text: Jody Scheckter is the South African driver who was the last Ferrari world champion before Michael Schumacher ended the 21-year drought. Won the 1979 title and then Ferrari didn't win another championship until the Schumacher era began in 2000.

name: Alan Jones
vibe_embedding_text: Alan Jones is the tough, hard-racing Australian who won the 1980 World Championship for Williams. Known for aggressive, no-nonsense driving and being one of the hardest racers of his era. Australia's first F1 world champion.

name: Phil Hill
vibe_embedding_text: Phil Hill is the first American-born Formula 1 World Champion, winning the 1961 title with Ferrari. A thoughtful, cultured driver in an era of great danger, his championship was overshadowed by the death of teammate Wolfgang von Trips at the same race.

name: Jack Brabham
vibe_embedding_text: Jack Brabham is the legendary Australian driver who built his own car and won the World Championship with it — the only driver-constructor champion in F1 history. Three-time world champion and engineering genius who founded the Brabham racing team.

name: Jim Clark
vibe_embedding_text: Jim Clark is the quiet Scottish farmer turned two-time World Champion, widely considered the most naturally gifted driver in F1 history. Won races by minutes with effortless smoothness in his Lotus. Tragically killed racing at Hockenheim 1968 at just 32 years old.

name: Graham Hill
vibe_embedding_text: Graham Hill is the only driver to complete motorsport's Triple Crown — winning the F1 World Championship, Indianapolis 500, and Le Mans 24 Hours. Two-time F1 champion, five-time Monaco winner, and father of future champion Damon Hill. The ultimate complete racing driver.

name: John Surtees
vibe_embedding_text: John Surtees is the only person to win World Championships on both two wheels and four wheels — MotoGP champion turned 1964 F1 World Champion with Ferrari. A unique athletic achievement that will likely never be repeated in motorsport.

name: Jochen Rindt
vibe_embedding_text: Jochen Rindt is F1's only posthumous World Champion — killed during practice at Monza 1970 but his points lead was never overhauled, sealing the title after his death. A fearless, spectacular Austrian driver whose legacy is tinged with tragedy.

name: Gilles Villeneuve
vibe_embedding_text: Gilles Villeneuve is the fearless, spectacular Canadian racing driver who drove with absolutely zero self-preservation. Father of Jacques Villeneuve, he never won a championship but is considered one of the most exciting drivers ever for his sideways, ragged-edge style. Killed at Zolder 1982.
